title: 2022 AMC 12A Problem 23
statement:
Let \(h_n\) and \(k_n\) be the unique relatively prime positive integers such that

\[\frac11+\frac12+\frac13+\cdots+\frac1n=\frac{h_n}{k_n}.\]

Let \(L_n\) denote the least common multiple of the numbers \(1,\) \(2,\) \(3,\) \(\ldots,\) \(n.\) For how many integers \(n\) with \(1\le n\le22\) is \(k_n\lt L_n?\)

solutions.text:
\(L_n\) is always divisible by \(k_n,\) so \(k_n\lt L_n\) exactly when some prime \(p\) divides both \(L_n\) and the numerator \(N=\sum_{k=1}^n \tfrac{L_n}{k}\) (i.e. a prime cancels).

For a prime \(p\) with maximal power \(p^a\le n,\) only the terms with \(v_p(k)=a\) keep \(p\) out of \(\frac{L_n}{k};\) all others are divisible by \(p.\) So \(p\) cancels iff \(\sum_{v_p(k)=a}\tfrac{L_n}{k}\equiv0\pmod p.\)

Applying this test recursively with \(H_n=H_{n-1}+\frac{1}{n}\) gives \(k_n=L_n\) for \(1\le n\le5,\) \(k_n=\frac{L_n}{3}\) for \(6\le n\le8,\) and \(k_n=L_n\) again for \(9\le n\le17.\) Finally, the ratios \(\frac{L_n}{k_n}\) for \(n=18,19,20,21,22\) are \(3,3,15,45,45,\) respectively. Thus cancellation occurs precisely for \(n=6,7,8,18,19,20,21,22,\) which is \(8\) values.

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Writing \(H_n\) over \(L_n,\) the reduced denominator is smaller exactly when a prime cancels from the numerator \(\sum_k \frac{L_n}{k}\)
For a prime power \(p^a\) with \(p^a\le n\lt p^{a+1},\) check whether \(p\) divides \(\sum_{v_p(k)=a} \frac{L_n}{k}\)
